newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BLOODIED ZARAGOZA KEEPS TITLE ON SPLIT DECISION.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BLOODIED ZARAGOZA KEEPS TITLE ON SPLIT DECISION.

text.p: Mexico's Daniel Zaragoza narrowly retained his World Boxing Council junior batamweight title by scoring a split decision win over Ireland's Wayne McCullough in a bloody slugfest on Saturday.
One judge had McCullough winning by a score of 114-115, but the other two scored the fight 116-112 for Zaragoza, who at 39 is the oldest reigning world champion in boxing.
"He put a lot of pressure on me in the last two rounds," said Zaragoza, who was impressed by the 26-year-old McCullough's conditioning. "I don't have his energy.
"I would fight him again any time. He's not a better fighter, but he is very strong."

With Boston's huge Irish-American population the crowd of 3,100 was heavily pro-McCullough. But few left disappointed and nearly everyone was on their feet screaming in the closing rounds as the two battered each other mercilessly, both covered with blood.
Zaragoza, who has not lost since 1993, improved to 54-7-3, while McCullough suffered his first loss, dropping to 20-1.
McCullough appeared to hold the advantage in the early rounds as Zaragoza bided his time before methodically working on the challenger.
By the fifth round Zaragoza was demonstrating his experience, letting McCullough come at him while smartly defending and counterpunching.
McCullough managed to back Zaragoza into the ropes a handful of times during the fight but was never able to put the champion away.
The middle rounds belonged to Zaragoza, who landed far more punches although he failed to dominate McCullough, a silver medalist at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics.
McCullough, his left eye nearly closed, came on strong in the final two rounds, picking up some badly needed points and making the bout almost too close to call.
By the end both fighters were in the middle of the ring, giving it everything they had left with both bleeding from the head.
"The last two rounds were unbelievable," McCullough said.
"I really thought I had it. He's a tough fighter. He didn't hurt me, but he busted me up a bit."
